expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: A deploy isn't atomic — for a window, old pods/processes are still running against the new schema. If the column drops before every instance is running the code that stopped reading it, those old instances start erroring.

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: Ship the code-only change today. Deploy it. Let it run…Then drop the column in its own migration, its own PR, its own deploy.

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: The DROP COLUMN is the irreversible step. Restore path = a database backup/snapshot restore. If someone later needs legacy_email, it's gone.

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: A code revert is a 20-minute fix any day of the week. A dropped column that turns out to matter needs a DB restore, ideally with someone who knows the restore procedure awake and available.

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: Friday afternoon is a bad time to need that person [who knows the restore procedure].

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: Offers to help check what CI guard would catch this ('ops mode has a device for that') but does not recommend adding one.

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: Short answer: don't merge it as one PR, and don't drop the column this afternoon regardless.

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: Reversible: the code changes that stop reading legacy_email. Irreversible: the DROP COLUMN.
